The user‐controlled servletPath and pathInfo are concatenated into a resource path without any strict base‐directory prefix enforcement. Although UriPath.canonical is called, it only handles null or empty and does not remove “..” segments; StringUtils.cleanPath normalizes the syntax but preserves leading “..” when there are too many, so “/../etc/passwd” remains “/../etc/passwd”. No check is made to ensure the final path stays within the intended classpath base. As a result, an attacker can supply traversal sequences and break out of the intended resource root, making this a real CWE-022 path traversal vulnerability.

That method converts backslashes, strips any URI prefix, handles leading slashes, splits on “/”, and processes “.” and “..” segments by removing or collapsing them. As a result “/static/../secret” becomes “/secret”, preventing directory traversal outside the intended classpath namespace. No other raw file system APIs are used, and ClassLoader.getResource only loads from the classpath. Therefore an attacker cannot traverse outside the served resources, making this finding a false positive.
